outOfScope: Unbounded autonomous product decisions and expansion beyond the supported delivery profile.
Replacing delivered Integration or Oracle authority contracts.
Treating this research allocation as implementation readiness or product delivery.
constraints: Research must compare reuse and the smallest existing-Core approach, inspect primary sources and pin selected versions before READY.
Future dependency plans are assumptions, not delivered truth; worker execution requires delivered dependencies and a current Jev-satisfied plan.
Real-provider and live-product evidence must be identified separately from deterministic mocks; no fabricated API runs, costs or judgments.
invariants: Application owns work semantics and domain authority; Oracle owns source IO; runtime success is not acceptance or publication authority.
Every result binds exact source, attempt, configuration and evidence; unknown effects or missing evidence cannot be called success.
The outer Blackboard schedules ExHarness development only; product runtime coordination remains a separate system.
architectureDecisions: D1 — BB-074 measures delivery-harness value using the unified benchmark contract; a direct-agent matched pilot is only one comparison, not the entire benchmark.
D2 — Use two workload classes: an external/public harness workload for external validity and ExHarness delivery-lifecycle scenarios for orchestration/recovery/currentness value.
D3 — Fixed-factor harness comparisons keep model snapshot, prompt/task input, starting workspace, resource ceilings, artifact extraction and evaluator constant.

D4 — Lifecycle scenarios include verifier repair, stale context, crash/resume, handoff, provider ambiguity, CI failure and authority/currentness fencing; do not invent fake symmetry where a direct harness lacks the capability.
D5 — Report accepted quality, economics, lead time, human active effort, consistency, robustness, recovery and failure fingerprints as a vector; no opaque ExHarness score.
implementationSlices: S1 — Bind BB-065/077/081 benchmark contracts and select external plus lifecycle workloads.
S2 — Define auditable human-effort measurement, repeats/sample policy, reset/leakage and decision gates.
S3 — Implement external fixed-factor comparison and lifecycle fault/recovery scenarios with complete attempt accounting.
S4 — Produce multidimensional value evidence and explicit pass/no-go/inconclusive outcome for downstream BB-075/076.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: External harness comparison holds all non-harness factors fixed and reports complete attempts with independent quality.
Delivery-lifecycle scenarios exercise repair, stale-state rejection, recovery/handoff, provider/CI failure and authority fencing with exact evidence.
Value is reported as a multidimensional quality/economics/time/human-effort/robustness profile with preregistered gates and uncertainty.

invariantCoverage.invariant: Application owns work semantics and domain authority; Oracle owns source IO; runtime success is not acceptance or publication authority.
Every result binds exact source, attempt, configuration and evidence; unknown effects or missing evidence cannot be called success.
The outer Blackboard schedules ExHarness development only; product runtime coordination remains a separate system.

researchGaps: Define the unified benchmark program from current harness-evaluation research: external/public harness workload, ExHarness delivery-lifecycle workload, held-out set and exact separation between them.
Freeze the experimental unit so model snapshot, prompt, task input, initial workspace, tool/resource ceilings, artifact extraction and evaluator are identical across harness arms.

Define comparison arms that include a minimal/direct baseline and ExHarness, plus component ablations where attribution is required; avoid a single Direct-vs-ExHarness aggregate as the only experiment.
Predeclare repeated-run policy, uncertainty reporting and fault injections for provider ambiguity, tool failure, process restart, stale state, CI failure, handoff and recovery.

Define the multidimensional result profile: accepted quality, cost/tokens per accepted delivery, latency, human active effort, consistency, robustness and failure fingerprints; do not collapse into one opaque score.
Pin the neutral execution/evaluation substrate and adapter implementation, including Harbor adoption or a documented rejection.
Rebind BB-075/076 to the resulting benchmark contract and obtain a fresh Jev readiness judgment after all gaps are resolved.
negativeVerificationCases: Producer success with failing independent acceptance.
Missing or stale source/runtime identity represented as current evidence.
Unresolved external effect retried as if confirmed safe.

laneContracts.input: exact READY plan + DONE direct dependencies
laneContracts.convergence: all acceptance claims SATISFIED + evaluated source merged

livingDocs.statement: BB-074 Living truth describes only the implemented and independently verified supported capability and limitations.
